items.title: George P. Fleming Interview, 1984-10-06
items.q: There was Oliver Alcorn. There was Alvin Alcorn's brother. He came out with the band during that time.

ctx.x: Did you lose touch with them? Not many. With that whole scene?

Not many really out here now that I grew up. There's one Tom Johnson. He's not playing anymore at the time. But he's out here. He came out here pretty. A lot of them came out with the bands, with the Navy band during the war. And they had a lot of New Orleans bands at the Treasure Island that came out here. I think even Willie Humphrey came out here with the band at that time during the war. And that's when I saw some of them. There was Oliver Alcorn. There was Alvin Alcorn's brother. He came out with the band…

Yeah. That's Alcorn. How do you spell it? A-L-C-R-N? Yeah. So now you're pretty much, though, in those days, a swing trumpet player. I mean, you were playing kind of with big bands. This was a lot different than what you grew up, the style you played in New Orleans. Yeah.
